title: Alivardi Khan Becomes Nawab
subtitle: Alivardi Khan Becomes Nawab
summary: In 1740, Alivardi Khan defeated Sarfaraz Khan and took power in Bengal, opening a nawabi phase defined by military pressure, Maratha incursions, and attempts to defend provincial autonomy.
heroTagline: Alivardi Khan Becomes Nawab reshaped power and governance patterns in Bengal.
whyItMatters: Alivardi's accession matters because it set the political and military context for the Bargi raids, the succession of Siraj ud-Daulah, and Bengal's vulnerability in the decade before Plassey.
longTermLegacy: His rule is remembered as a period of defensive statecraft under pressure, bridging late Mughal provincial autonomy and the crisis that culminated in 1757.
identityMemoryNotes: Alivardi Khan's memory often appears through the linked stories of Maratha raids, Siraj ud-Daulah, and the coming Company conflict.

claimCitations.claim: In 1740, Alivardi Khan defeated Sarfaraz Khan and took power in Bengal, opening a nawabi phase defined by military pressure, Maratha incursions, and attempts to defend provincial autonomy.
Alivardi's accession matters because it set the political and military context for the Bargi raids, the succession of Siraj ud-Daulah, and Bengal's vulnerability in the decade before Plassey.
His rule is remembered as a period of defensive statecraft under pressure, bridging late Mughal provincial autonomy and the crisis that culminated in 1757.
Alivardi Khan's memory often appears through the linked stories of Maratha raids, Siraj ud-Daulah, and the coming Company conflict.
